reason: (1) The mechanism premise is false by measurement. K6's anchor stage is not bound by a GIL-held blake2b loop: there are only ~99-121 anchors per frame (G-A: 1,965,923 anchors / 19,900 frames; local 121). A local benchmark of wt5 tools/overlap_reg.py (sparse path, 4 visible clips, 25 frames each) splits sequential time as read 4.24 s + filter 6.99 s + hash 0.08 s: hashing is 0.7%. ThreadPoolExecutor(4) ran 3.06x faster than sequential (0.039 s/frame wall) and beat a spawn Pool(4) (2.70x). On cold frames threads still ran 1.58x faster than warm sequential. (2) The actionable part, MAX_S = 3600, duplicates sibling PC8-03, which already proposes it together with a G-D projection from the dummy log. (3) The new part, r = K6/probe measured on the 4 visible clips and applied to the probe's hidden latency, adds noise and does not add safety. 400 frames are dominated by fixed costs (spawn start, CUDA init). L_probe_hi also contains container start, scoring and poll granularity. Hidden-run logs cannot be read, so 'log s/frame in both logs' works only on dummies, and K6 already prints frames and anchor seconds (wt5 build_probe_kernel.py l.2108). The ratio would also make the K6 submit wait on the G-P read. (4) BUDGET_S 33000 + MAX_S 3600 gives a worst-case end of 10.17 h: that stays under the 12 h Kaggle limit but exceeds the 9.5 h R5(a) limit that G-LB requires. (5) The line itself defaults to STOP: G-A FAILED as pre-registered (ga_report.json G_A_pass=false, 43/62 < 60; PC8-01 confirmed). The fix therefore matters only after a logged post-hoc user 'continue'. Still, the underlying risk is real: 20k hidden frames x 0.12 s/frame single-thread x 1.5-2 Kaggle slowdown = 3,600-4,800 s, or <= ~3,000 s with thread scaling >= 1.6x. MAX_S 1800 could therefore trip 'SKIPPED (time)' at the Data-page size, while ~10k frames (step 0) fit (<= ~1,500 s).
fix: Merge into PC8-03 and drop the ratio rule. Before any K6 dummy push, and only if the user logs a post-hoc 'continue' after the G-A FAIL, set the stage knobs unconditionally: BIOHUB_OVERLAPCONS_MAX_S=3600 and BIOHUB_OVERLAPCONS_BUDGET_S=30600, so the worst-case end is <= 34,200 s = 9.5 h (R5(a)). K2's writer finishes at ~7.3-7.5 h, so the start margin stays >= ~1 h. G-D criterion: from the dummy log line 'OVERLAPCONS registration: ... frames N ... anchors Xs verify Ys', project (X + Y) x 20,000 / N x 2 (Kaggle and cold-I/O factor) and require <= MAX_S. If it fails, switch _OcPool to the spawn process pool used by G-P (already tested) instead of raising MAX_S further. Leave the 12 h hard limit and the finals #37 + #38 untouched. Do not make any knob depend on a hidden-run latency.
realistic_gain: About 0 on score. It removes a tail risk (a silent K6 == K2 when the hidden set is ~20k frames) in a line whose expected gain is <= +0.0005 and which by default stops after the G-A FAIL. The measurement's real value is that it removes the GIL worry: threads scale ~3x warm and ~1.6x cold, and hashing is <1% of the stage.
